newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-COUNTRY, HANSAPANK GET RATINGS FROM THOMSON.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-COUNTRY, HANSAPANK GET RATINGS FROM THOMSON.

text.p: Thomson BankWatch said on Wednesday that it had assigned Estonia a soverign risk rating of BBB-.
Thomson also said in a statement that it had assigned Estonia's leading bank, Hansapank, an intra-country issuer rating of IC-B and a short-term local currecny debt rating of LC-1.
A Hansapank official told Reuters that Thomson had initiated the ratings itself.
Thomson said that Estonia's rating was based on "the country's remarkable economic transformation since its independence from the former Soviet Union."
"Economic output has accelerated...buoyed by rising domestic demand, mounting tourism revenues, and increasing foreign investment," Thomson said.

"It (Estonia) has achieved solid progress in the transition to a market-based economy and clearly warrents an investment-grade rating," Betty J. Starkey, the director of sovereign risk at Thomson, was quoted as saying.
However, she cautioned that the country still faced tough challenges stemming from its small size, growing trade imbalance, rigid exchange rate regime, and potential bugdetary pressures.
